I am sixty years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou since I was a girl. I never went to school, but I know this land by touch and by season. My son works in a factory in Handan, so most days it is just me and my old ox. We have about eight mu of good flat land on the North China Plain.

The wheat is already in the ground — I sowed Luyuan502 last October after rotary tillage. It is a reliable improved variety that my neighbors also use. I gave it winter irrigation before the frost, and I topdressed with urea just after Qingming. Now, in late April, the wheat is jointing. I will irrigate it once more when the heads are filling, and if May turns dry, I will water again. I already sprayed herbicide in early spring, and I watch for aphids and rust. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant Denghai605 maize the same day. We do not till for maize anymore — we drill the seed straight into the wheat stubble. It saves my back and the seed is good hybrid seed from the co-op. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting, then side-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. The maize will need two irrigations, one at jointing and one at tasseling, and I will spray for corn borer and armyworm twice, plus one herbicide spray. I expect around 570 kg per mu.

I have thought about cotton or vegetables, but at my age I do not have the strength for all that weeding and the endless pesticide spraying that cotton needs. Wheat and maize are steady. The grain station buys my wheat, and the feed mill takes the maize. It is enough to live on and to help my grandson with school fees.
